accessibility.text: two arguments against free will
is fate real?
three ways out
The fatalist argument
1. We have no choice about past facts.
2. In the past, there were truths about our future actions.
3. We have no choice about the truth that in the future I will perform a certain action. (1,2)
4. If we have no choice about some facts, and those facts necessitate X, we have no choice about X.
5. It being true that we will perform some action necessitates that we will perform that action.
C. We have no choice about whether we will perform our future actions. (3,4,5)
The foreknowledge argument

why believe in free will?
Like the Foreknowledge Argument, the Fatalist Argument is a serious challenge to the reality of freedom of the will.
1. We have no choice about past facts.
2. In the past, God had foreknowledge of our future actions.
3. We have no choice about the fact that God knows that in the future I will perform a certain action. (1,2)
4. If we have no choice about some facts, and those facts necessitate X, we have no choice about X.
5. God knowing that we will perform some action necessitates that we will perform that action.
C. We have no choice about whether we will perform our future actions. (3,4,5)
But before we do that, let’s ask: can we come up with an argument similar to the Foreknowledge Argument which is based, not on foreknowledge, but on fate?
